newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by firm demand from packers who saw operating margins move into profitable territory Friday, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $60.00, Illinois top hogs were expected at $60.00-$60.50 and Indiana/Ohio top hog prices were seen at $60.00-$60.25.
Expected gains could be offset by increased marketings if Midwest heat and humidity come down, sources said.
Support also could be limited by outlooks for light slaughter on Monday, including the closure of two large hog plants due to a floating holiday, they said.

Farmland Industries' Dubuque, Iowa, hog plant, with an estimated daily slaughter capacity of 10,000 head, and ConAgra Inc's subsidiary Swift and Co.'s Marshalltown, Iowa, plant, with an estimated capacity of 14,000-16,000 head, will be closed because of a floating holiday, company sources said.
American Foods Group Inc's Dakota Pork Industries plant in Huron, S.D., with a capacity near 7,500 head, will be closed after the plant went to a four-day week, a plant source said.
